headline: High: dexter’s broad egress and secrets handling can collide with marketingskills’ writable workspace, creating default data-leak and action-conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter can read/write .dexter/scratchpad and uses autonomous execution, while marketingskills explicitly uses shared-context skills files. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if one agent consumes the other’s files as prompts. No direct parser proof is present, so I choose medium rather than low.
conditions: IF either agent ingests the other’s workspace files as prompt text, injection becomes active.
IF the shared-context skills files are treated as authoritative instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Disable automatic prompt loading from shared files.
Add a manual review step before one agent consumes the other’s outputs.
Prefix imported content as untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent file reads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter handles financial data and broad network egress plus multiple external APIs, while marketingskills has filesystem read/write and allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive financial or marketing context can flow into dexter’s third-party calls or logs. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents share any filesystem path, files touched by one can be read by the other.
IF dexter sends workspace content to OpenAI, Exa, Tavily, or Financial Datasets APIs, that content leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace.
Remove sensitive files from shared directories.
Restrict dexter API inputs to minimal prompts.
Audit outbound requests for file-content payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marketingskills can read and write files and spawn subprocesses, while dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution with filesystem scratchpad use. Overlapping writes to shared files or generated artifacts can race and corrupt state. No locking mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF either agent launches subprocesses that mutate shared artifacts, race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Make generated filenames unique per agent.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter can generate research outputs from external APIs, and marketingskills is designed around shared-context skills that may reuse prior outputs. If marketingskills treats dexter’s output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream marketing content. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes dexter-generated claims without verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF dexter’s API-derived outputs are reused as source material, downstream content may inherit errors.
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse.
Add a human review gate for factual claims.
Mark dexter outputs as draft only.
Compare claims against primary sources.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-validation before reuse.

E_compliance.rationale: dexter touches financial data and requests many external API keys, while marketingskills stores product-marketing context in local skill files. If regulated financial or personal data is placed into dexter and then mirrored into marketingskills files, retention and residency controls may diverge. No explicit compliance certifications are documented for either agent, so uncertainty remains medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial or personal data is stored in shared skill files, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF either agent logs or exports data to a third-party service, residency and retention obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files.
Document retention rules for each workspace.
Limit API-key scope to least privilege.
Review whether any data class is subject to special handling.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data routing and retention enforcement.
